newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland's PBK may be worth PLN 1.2-1.6 bln - HSBC.
newsitem.headline: Poland's PBK may be worth PLN 1.2-1.6 bln - HSBC.

text.p: HSBC Investment Services, picked to advise Poland in the privatisation of its Powszechny Bank Kredytowy SA (PBK) bank, estimates its value at 1.2-1.6 billion zlotys, the head of the HSBC Polish unit said on Wednesday.
Hubert Janiszewski told Reuters the estimate was based on the preliminary analysis of the bank's half-year performance and earnings forecasts for the whole of 1996.
"Our very early rough estimate puts the value of the company at 1.2-1.6 billion zlotys and it is based on the half year results and expected 1996 earnings," Janiszewski said.
"This can be adjusted both down or up depending on the year-end results and first quarter performance," he added.
Finance Ministry announced on Monday it had picked HSBC as its advisor in a tender.
PBK, one of the nine commercial banks created on the basis of former central bank branches in 1989 will be the fifth one to be privatised.

It had a net profit of 185.17 million zlotys after the first nine months of this year against 121.07 for the whole of 1995. Its balance sheet total after the nine months of this year is 8.37 billion zlotys against 7.37 billion in 1995.

Janiszewski said that under the tender's conditions the adviser would place 65 percent of PBK through an offer to a selected investor or a group of investors and would later set a public offering of a further 15 percent of the bank's shares.
He said the public offer would hit the market no sooner than the fourth quarter of 1997.
"In my opinion the public offering will enter the market no sooner than in October 1997," Janiszewski said.
He said several foreign and domestic investors were interested in PBK but declined to elaborate.
Poland's listed banks Kredyt Bank and Polish Development Bank have signalled their interest in participating in PBK's privatisation.
A banking official, who declined to be named, told Reuters, that among institutions interested in the PBK privatisation were also Citibank, Chase Manhattan Bank and Bank of Tokyo.
Janiszewski said he was aware of such speculation but declined comment.
